newsitem.title: UK: Dixons up as retail sector rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Dixons up as retail sector rebounds.

text.p: Shares in Dixons Group Plc rose in a firm stores sector on Tuesday, as a short position in the market squeezed the stock higher and retailers bounced back from recent weakness, traders said.

One cited the British Retail Consortium's October survey showing a rebound in electrical and electronic goods following a dip in September as being potentially positive for Dixons in the run-up to Christmas.
Dixons shares were up 16-1/2p at 564 by 0930 GMT, rebounding towards its record 589p set October 24.
Elswhere in the stores sector, Great Universal Stores Plc was up 7p at 590-1/2, Marks & Spencer Plc was up 3p at 487 and Boots Co Plc was up 5-1/2p at 616-1/2.
"The sector has been weak recently and looks as if it is turning a bit better," said one trader. "It is attracting a bit of money."
The British Retail Consortium Survey said sales picked up in October after easing slightly in September, though there was no sign of a return of the 1980s consumer boom.
On electrical and electronic goods, it said sales improved after a dip in September with PCs the star performer.

"White goods, TVs and videos all increased reasonably and sales of hi-fi were relatively buoyant," the BRC said. It was "generally quite a satisfactory month and a useful start for the run-up to Christmas."

Traders at several top securities houses said they were unaware of any other specific reasons for the sharp rise in Dixons shares but one said a early demand for the stock had caught one market-maker short of stock.
"It was strong before the opening and that exacerbated a short position," said a trader at one leading brokerage.
